significance.root_decision: The conjecture holds: for 1 ≤ k ≤ n−1, the pair (k, n) is inadmissible exactly when n ≥ 13, n ≡ 1 (mod 6) and k = 2 or k = n−2. There are two halves. Exclusion, for every such n (the source had it only up to n = 31, by exhaustive computation): a Littlewood polynomial with no zero on the circle and exactly two zeros inside is coprime to its reciprocal, so its Schur–Cohn form is nonsingular with exactly two negative directions; the tree of sign prefixes that survive this test is small and repeats with period 12, which is carried to every depth by stationary submatrices and 60 kernel vectors, and every completed word is excluded by an exact certificate. This half is computer-assisted: about 32,000 certificate cases, all checked in the Lean kernel together with proofs that they cover every case. Existence, for every other pair: most cases are theorems of the source; the remaining cases (even k ≥ 12 in two ranges) are filled by a new family of polynomials, whose zero counts are proved in Lean by a root-counting argument on arcs and a strict-dominance comparison. Lean defines Littlewood polynomials (all coefficients ±1), the count of zeros in the open disc with multiplicity, and admissibility literally, proves the Schur–Cohn root count from scratch, and proves the classification from five results of the source taken as explicit hypotheses.
significance.caveat: Five results of the source are links outside Lean, taken as explicit hypotheses of the Lean theorem: Proposition 2.6 (Mukunda), Theorems 2.7, 2.8 and 2.9, and Corollary 2.11; the source's proofs of Theorems 2.7 and 2.8 are themselves computer-assisted. The final check confirmed that each is the source's printed statement and verified all five by exact computation (every Littlewood polynomial up to degree 19; the witness families up to degree 64). Most of the existence half therefore comes from the source; the new existence content is one even-k family, and the new exclusion content is the statement for every n beyond 31. The exclusion proof is computer-assisted (a finite exact certificate plus a period-12 induction), replayed in the Lean kernel in 11,479 modules (about 604,000 generated lines). Root's rebuild needed more memory than the standard runner allows for one assembly module (Lean's heap threshold raised from 3,500 MB to 14,000 MB for the last three modules; a resource setting that does not affect what the kernel checks). The source's definition of Littlewood polynomials omits the constant coefficient from the ±1 condition; this is a typo (the source's tables and computations use all coefficients ±1), and the result is for that class. The first reviewer closed one small gap in the written proof. The journal version (Math. Comp. 2021) was not read (reviewer's probability that it changes anything: about 0.03). All work is by AI and no human has checked it: the proof, the Lean code and the paper are by GPT-6.2 Sol lanes; the adversarial review before Lean (not routine 0.85) and the final check (0.80) are by two separate Claude Opus 5.5 lanes.
